Hubs, agents and sub-agents

A hub groups related agents. Each agent does one business task, and every agent runs the same four sub-agents in order. The result can go to a dashboard, a report, an export file or your ERP.

03 · business rules

Rule sets in four types

A rule is a calculation, a validation, a transformation or an assignment, and rules are grouped into named rule sets. Describe the rule in plain language and the platform drafts it. A person reviews the draft before it is saved.

04 · access

Roles and visibility tiers

Roles carry named permissions. A case is general, protected, or restricted to one owner, and only the current holder of a case can act on it. An administrator override exists, but only as an explicit permission you grant, and it never reaches a restricted case.

Try the roles in Governance

05 · delegation

Tasks without handing over the case

The holder delegates tasks and keeps the case. Each task has a deadline that cannot pass the case deadline, and moves from open to completed, with send-back and resubmission in between. A case cannot close while a task is still open.

Open
Submitted
Sent back
Resubmitted
Completed

06 · audit and notifications

A log nobody can edit

Every action is written to a read-only activity log with the actor and a timestamp. It cannot be edited or deleted. Watchers are told about each change in the app and by email, and they cannot act on the case.
